chapter: Army, return to El Paso and Mardi Gras parades
title: The Zulu parade route as printed versus as marched
summary: Alfred and Allen compare the route printed in the paper with the route the Zulu parade took.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: The paper said they was going down Cleveland to St. Benard, then back up on the uptown side, St. Benard, to Portris, South Portris, to Simon Bolivar. Through those pass up right on up Simon Bolivar. To Jackson, back Jackson to Magnolia. Down Magnolia to Melton-Mead. Back out Melton-Mead and Simon Bolivar, this band. That's what I read, see. Yeah. But they say it was all together different.

They made it up, I think, more or less by the route, because I caught them on a cell in Ohio Street. They made their turn at Louisiana. That's where I rode with Louis Haney and Melvin Green in the captain's car. Because I remember that, and I remember getting into the car. I remember a good bit.
Well, they went to Luzon Avenue.
Yeah, and turned around on my cell, and that was what the paper said.
And come back down my cell.
Come back down my cell. And then I...

I got off from watching the Luzon Avenue on the bus. Oh, you don't know where then went. I was so tired then. But you know, that's what the paper said. They were doing it like that. That's what they said. But I guess they broke up.
